name: Executive order of April 9, 1874 setting apart lands for the Muckleshoot reservation
promises: Not a cession: the President set apart certain lands for a reservation, supplemental to the executive order of January 20, 1857 (Royce p. 872).

Royce: this constitutes the present Muckleshoot reservation, sections 2 and 12 of T. 20 N., R. 5 E., and sections 20, 28 and 34 of T. 21 N., R. 5 E., Willamette meridian, within territory first ceded by the Dwamish and others on January 22, 1855 (p. 873, area 564).
landTaken: None by this order; it set land apart for the reservation.
today: Royce (1899) records that these sections constitute the present Muckleshoot reservation.

sources.title: Charles C. Royce, Indian Land Cessions in the United States (18th Annual Report of the Bureau of American Ethnology, 1899), schedule pp. 872-873, executive order of April 9, 1874, area 564

openQuestions: The Muckleshoot claim before the Indian Claims Commission (Docket 98, decisions of 1953 and 1955) concerns aboriginal land ceded under the 1855 Point Elliott treaty, not this order; it was listed but not read.
Allotment and later loss of land inside the reservation were not researched.
No Muckleshoot account of this order was looked up in this pass.

treaties.json also has cession-1857-01-20-muckleshoot-reservation for the 1857 order (same area 564), which has no findings file yet. treaties.json lists no presentDayTribes for this record. Not edited.
